examples.ko: 강아지를 하루 종일 굶기면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not leave a puppy without food all day.
No parent lets their child go hungry.
I was busy yesterday and left my cat without food.
No matter how angry you are, don't make your child go hungry.
I didn't mean to make my little brother go hungry.

examples.ko: 벌로 밥을 굶기는 건 좋은 교육이 아니에요.
examples.en: Making a child skip meals as punishment is not good parenting.

explain: '굶다'는 내가 먹지 않는 것이고, 굶기다는 다른 사람이나 동물을 먹지 못하게 하는 거예요. '밥을 굶다'와 '아이를 굶기다'를 구분해서 써요.

phrases.en: Please don't let the cat go hungry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부탁이나 주의를 줄 때 쓰는 존댓말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to ask or warn someone.

phrases.en: I was busy and made my child skip lunch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형이고, 의도하지 않았어도 먹이지 못한 상황에 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past tense; it can describe failing to feed someone even unintentionally.

phrases.en: I work hard so that my child doesn't go hungry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 쓰면 먹을 것을 꼭 챙겨 준다는 뜻이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form means making sure someone gets enough to eat.

explain_en: '굶다' is when you yourself go without eating, while 굶기다 means making another person or animal go without food. Compare '밥을 굶다' with '아이를 굶기다'.

examples.en: The rice cake is soft and squishy, so it's nice to eat.
This jelly is soft and chewy, so kids like it.
Please knead the dough until it becomes soft.
The freshly baked bread is soft and warm.
Squeezing a stress ball softly makes me feel better.

examples.ko: 머리가 말랑말랑한 어릴 때 외국어를 배우면 좋아요.
examples.en: It's good to learn a foreign language while young, when the mind is still flexible.

explain: 손으로 눌렀을 때 부드럽고 탄력 있는 느낌이에요. '딱딱하다'의 반대로 떡, 젤리, 빵, 찰흙에 잘 써요. 생각이 유연하다는 뜻으로 '말랑말랑한 머리'처럼 비유로도 쓰고, 일상에서는 '말랑말랑하다' 꼴이 더 자주 들려요.

phrases.en: This bread is very soft and springy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '말랑말랑' 대신 '하다'가 붙은 꼴이 더 자주 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily speech the 하다 form is heard more often than the bare adverb.

phrases.en: I like soft, squishy jelly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에 쓰면 먹거나 만지는 것의 느낌을 설명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a noun it describes how something feels to eat or touch.

phrases.en: Knead the dough until it becomes soft.
phrases.nuance_ko: 딱딱하던 것이 부드럽게 변하는 과정을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes something hard turning soft.

explain_en: It describes a soft, springy feel when pressed by hand, the opposite of '딱딱하다' (hard), and fits rice cakes, jelly, bread and clay. It can also describe a flexible mind, as in '말랑말랑한 머리'. In daily speech you hear the '말랑말랑하다' form more often.

examples.en: We grind red peppers to make chili powder.
My mother had rice ground at the mill and brought it back.
I use a mortar when I crush garlic.
Please grind the sesame seeds finely.
This machine grinds grain quickly.
I sprinkled the ground salt on the food.

explain: 곡식, 고추, 깨처럼 딱딱하거나 마른 것을 부수어 가루로 만들 때 써요. 절구로 콩이나 마늘을 두드려 부수는 건 '찧다'라고도 해요. 받침 'ㅎ' 때문에 '빻아요[빠아요]', '빻고[빠코]'처럼 발음이 달라지니 주의하세요.

phrases.en: I brought back grain I had ground at the mill.
phrases.nuance_ko: '빻다'와 가장 자주 같이 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common object paired with 'ppatta'.

phrases.en: I grind rice into flour and make rice cakes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결과가 가루가 된다는 점을 분명하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Makes clear that the result is powder.

phrases.en: I put the ground chili peppers into a jar.
phrases.nuance_ko: '빻다'의 활용형으로, 이미 가루로 만든 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A past modifier form for something that has already been ground.

explain_en: Use it when you break hard or dry things like grain, chili peppers or sesame seeds into powder. Pounding things such as garlic in a mortar can also be called '찧다'. Because of the final 'ㅎ', the pronunciation shifts in forms like '빻고[빠코]', so be careful.

examples.ko: 냉장고에 넣지 않으면 음식을 썩히게 돼요.
examples.en: If you don't put food in the fridge, you'll let it rot.
What a waste, I let all the fruit go bad.

examples.ko: 재능을 썩히지 말고 한번 도전해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't let your talent go to waste; give it a try.
We let fallen leaves rot and make fertilizer.
I'm letting good clothes sit unused in the wardrobe.

examples.ko: 화분에 물을 너무 많이 주면 뿌리를 썩혀요.
examples.en: If you water a plant too much, you make its roots rot.

explain: '썩다'에 시키는 뜻이 더해져 어떤 것이 썩도록 두거나 만든다는 말이에요. 쓸모 있는 재능이나 물건을 쓰지 않고 그냥 두는 것에도 '썩히다'를 써요. 걱정을 끼친다는 뜻의 '속을 썩이다'는 '썩이다'라고 써서 '썩히다'와 달라요.

phrases.en: It's a waste to let that talent go to waste.
phrases.nuance_ko: 능력을 쓰지 않고 그냥 둘 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an ability is left unused.

phrases.example: 쓰지 않는 물건을 썩혀 두지 마세요.
phrases.en: Don't leave things you don't use to waste.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쓸모 있는 것을 방치한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means leaving something useful unused.

phrases.en: I left the fruit too long and let it rot.
phrases.nuance_ko: '썩히다'를 풀어서 쓴 같은 뜻의 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The same meaning spelled out in two words.

explain_en: It is the causative of '썩다' (to rot), meaning to let something rot or make it rot. It is also used for leaving a useful talent or item unused. The idiom '속을 썩이다' (to cause someone worry) uses '썩이다', not '썩히다'.

examples.en: Plants get nutrients from the soil.

examples.ko: 이 죽에는 영양분이 많아서 아플 때 먹기 좋아요.
examples.en: This porridge is full of nutrients, so it's good when you're sick.
Babies get their nourishment from their mother's milk.

examples.ko: 오래 끓이면 영양분이 빠져나갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you boil it too long, the nutrients can be lost.
I bought fertilizer to feed my potted plant.
When I'm busy, it's hard to get enough nutrition.

explain: '영양'은 몸이 받는 전체 상태이고, '영양분'은 그 안에 들어 있는 성분 하나하나에 가까워요. '영양분이 많다/풍부하다', '영양분을 섭취하다/공급하다'처럼 써요. 식물에도 쓰고, 비슷한 말로 '영양소'가 있어요.

phrases.en: Spinach is a vegetable rich in nutrients.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식이나 흙에 영양 성분이 많다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say food or soil has plenty of nutrients.

phrases.example: 몸에 필요한 영양분을 골고루 섭취해야 해요.
phrases.en: You need to take in all the nutrients your body needs evenly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먹어서 영양분을 얻는다는 뜻으로, 조금 격식 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A slightly formal way to say getting nutrients by eating.

phrases.example: 밥에는 탄수화물 같은 영양소가 들어 있어요.
phrases.en: Rice contains nutrients such as carbohydrates.
phrases.nuance_ko: '영양분'과 비슷하고, 탄수화물·단백질처럼 종류를 말할 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 영양분, but used more when naming types like carbohydrates or protein.

explain_en: 영양 is the overall nutrition state, while 영양분 points more to the nutrient content itself. Common collocations are 영양분이 풍부하다 and 영양분을 섭취하다. It also works for plants, and 영양소 is a close synonym.

examples.en: The baby munches its food in small bites.
The rabbit is nibbling on a carrot.
I put candy in my mouth and rolled it around.

examples.ko: 아이가 오물오물 뭔가 말했는데 잘 안 들렸어요.
examples.en: The child mumbled something, but I couldn't hear it well.
The goldfish keeps moving its mouth.
Grandmother smiled while chewing slowly.

explain: '오물거리다'의 부사형으로, 작은 입이 계속 움직이는 모습을 말해요. '냠냠'처럼 소리를 흉내 내는 말이 아니라 입 모양이나 움직임을 보여 줘요.

phrases.en: The child chews the snack in small bites.
phrases.nuance_ko: '씹다'와 함께 쓰면 작은 입으로 천천히 씹는 모습이 그려져요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 'chew', it paints a picture of slow chewing with a small mouth.

phrases.en: The way the hamster munches is cute.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 '모습'을 붙여 귀여운 장면을 설명할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often followed by 'appearance' to describe a cute scene.

phrases.en: The baby moves its mouth while sleeping.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먹지 않을 때도 입이 계속 움직이는 모습에 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can describe a mouth that keeps moving even when not eating.

explain_en: It is the adverb form of '오물거리다' and shows a small mouth moving continuously. Unlike '냠냠', it does not imitate a sound but describes the mouth's movement.

examples.en: That chef is very quick with the knife.

examples.ko: 양파를 썰 때는 칼질을 천천히 해야 해요.
examples.en: When slicing onions, you have to cut slowly.

examples.ko: 도마에서 나는 칼질 소리가 규칙적으로 들려요.
examples.en: I hear the rhythmic sound of chopping on the cutting board.
My knife work is clumsy, so the carrots are uneven.
It looks cool to watch him cut on the cutting board.

examples.ko: 레스토랑에서 스테이크 칼질을 처음 해 봤어요.
examples.en: I cut a steak with a knife at a restaurant for the first time.

explain: 재료를 칼로 써는 동작이나 그 솜씨를 말해요. 솜씨를 말할 때는 '칼질이 빠르다/서툴다/능숙하다'처럼 써요. 칼로 써는 서양식 식사를 가볍게 '칼질'이라고 말하기도 해요.

phrases.example: 저는 칼질이 서툴러서 요리가 오래 걸려요.
phrases.en: I'm clumsy with a knife, so cooking takes a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 칼 쓰는 솜씨가 부족할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone lacks skill with a knife.

phrases.en: The chef is really skilled with a knife.
phrases.nuance_ko: 칼 쓰는 솜씨가 좋다고 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to praise someone's knife skills.

phrases.en: I carefully cut things on the cutting board.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재료를 써는 동작 자체를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the act of cutting ingredients itself.

explain_en: It refers to the act or skill of cutting food with a knife. For skill you say '칼질이 빠르다/서툴다/능숙하다'. People also casually call a knife-and-fork Western-style meal '칼질'.

examples.en: The city provides lunch to children who go without meals.
I worry that more children go hungry during vacation.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 교회는 결식아동을 위해 도시락을 만들어요.
examples.en: The church in our neighborhood makes lunch boxes for children who miss meals.
The meal support program for underfed children has been expanded.
The donations are used for the breakfasts of children who go without meals.

examples.ko: 결식아동도 눈치 보지 않고 밥을 먹을 수 있어야 해요.
examples.en: Children who miss meals should also be able to eat without feeling awkward.

explain: 뉴스나 복지 정책에서 주로 나오는 공식적인 말이에요. 대화에서는 '밥을 제대로 못 먹는 아이들'처럼 풀어서 말하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.example: 학교에서 결식아동 급식을 신청할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can apply for meal support for undernourished children at school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 복지 제도나 공지에서 자주 보는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase in welfare programs and notices.

phrases.example: 우리 반은 결식아동을 돕기 위해 모금했어요.
phrases.en: Our class raised money to help undernourished children.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기부나 봉사 이야기에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when talking about donations or volunteering.

phrases.example: 뉴스에서 밥을 제대로 못 먹는 아이들 이야기를 봤어요.
phrases.en: I saw a news story about children who can't eat properly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '결식아동'을 일상 대화에서 풀어서 말하는 쉬운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday way to explain '결식아동' in conversation.

explain_en: This is a formal term that mostly appears in the news and welfare policy. In conversation people often put it in plain words, like '밥을 제대로 못 먹는 아이들' (children who cannot eat properly).

en: to discourage; to daunt; to dishearten

examples.ko: 상대 팀 응원 소리가 우리를 기죽였어요.
examples.en: The other team's cheering intimidated us.
Don't discourage the child, encourage him.

examples.ko: 일부러 후배를 기죽이려고 한 말은 아니에요.
examples.en: I didn't say it on purpose to dishearten my junior.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 큰 덩치로 상대를 기죽여요.
examples.en: That player intimidates opponents with his big build.
Don't say things that bring your friend down.

examples.ko: 비싼 가방 자랑으로 사람들을 기죽이고 싶지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't want to make people feel small by showing off an expensive bag.

explain: '기죽다'의 사동 표현이라서 '누가 누구를 기죽이다' 모양으로 써요. '기를 죽이다'로도 말하고, 반대는 '기를 살려 주다'예요.

phrases.example: 큰 소리로 말해서 아이의 기를 죽이지 마세요.
phrases.en: Don't dishearten the child by speaking in a loud voice.
phrases.nuance_ko: '기죽이다'와 뜻이 같고, '기'와 '죽이다' 사이에 '를'을 넣어 쓴 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 기죽이다, with the particle 를 placed between 기 and 죽이다.

phrases.example: 기죽이는 말은 하지 않는 게 좋아요.
phrases.en: It's best not to say discouraging things.
phrases.nuance_ko: 듣는 사람의 자신감을 떨어뜨리는 말을 뜻해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Words that lower the listener's confidence.

phrases.en: One comment from my friend discouraged me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거에 있었던 일을 말할 때 쓰는 해요체예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Polite past form for something that happened.

explain_en: It is the causative form of '기죽다', so it is used in the pattern 'someone discourages someone'. It can also be said as '기를 죽이다', and the opposite is '기를 살려 주다' (to boost someone's spirits).

en: to bring dishonor to; to put someone to shame

examples.en: The child embarrassed their dad in front of the guests.
You shouldn't embarrass a friend on purpose.
Did you do that to embarrass me?
That person humiliated a team member in the meeting.
Don't do anything that shames your family.
If you're thinking of embarrassing me, stop.

explain: '망신시키다'는 일부러든 아니든 누군가를 남 앞에서 창피하게 만드는 거예요. 내가 스스로 망신을 겪는 '망신당하다'와 짝이에요. '가문을 망신시키다'처럼 가족이나 집단의 명예를 해칠 때도 써요.

phrases.en: Please don't embarrass me in front of people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대에게 창피하게 만들지 말라고 부탁하거나 화를 낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask or warn someone not to make you look bad.

phrases.en: The teacher humiliated the student in front of the class.
phrases.nuance_ko: '망신시키다'와 뜻이 같아요. '망신을 주다'가 말할 때 조금 더 자연스러운 경우가 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '망신시키다'; '망신을 주다' often sounds a bit more natural in speech.

phrases.en: I don't want to bring shame on my family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가족이나 집단의 명예를 해칠 때도 이렇게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used when damaging the honor of a family or group.
phrases.en_equiv: to bring shame on one's family

explain_en: 망신시키다 means making someone look bad in front of others, intentionally or not. It pairs with 망신당하다, where the person themselves goes through the shame. It is also used when someone damages the honor of a family or group.

examples.en: In the past there were many illiterate people.
Night schools taught reading and writing to illiterate people.

examples.ko: 그분은 어른이 되어서 문맹자 교실에 다니셨어요.
examples.en: He attended a literacy class as an adult.

examples.ko: 문맹자도 쉽게 이용할 수 있는 안내판이 필요해요.
examples.en: We need signs that even people who can't read can use easily.
I watched a documentary about the difficulties illiterate people face.

examples.ko: 이 마을에는 문맹자를 돕는 봉사 모임이 있어요.
examples.en: This village has a volunteer group that helps people who can't read.

explain: 글을 읽고 쓰지 못하는 사람을 가리키는 딱딱한 말이에요. 사람에게 직접 쓰면 기분 나쁠 수 있어서, 일상에서는 '글을 못 읽는 분'처럼 풀어서 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: There were many illiterate people in this village.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 곳에 글을 못 읽는 사람이 많다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Says that a place has many people who can't read.

phrases.en: Education for illiterate people is needed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글을 가르치는 교육을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for education that teaches reading and writing.

phrases.en: I helped a person who can't read.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람에게 말할 때는 이렇게 풀어서 부드럽게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A softer way to say it when talking about a person.

explain_en: This is a formal word for someone who cannot read or write. Using it directly about a person can sound unkind, so in daily speech people may say it in a softer way, like '글을 못 읽는 분'.

examples.ko: 민초들의 삶은 예나 지금이나 쉽지 않았어요.
examples.en: The lives of ordinary people have never been easy.

examples.ko: 이 소설은 이름 없는 민초들의 이야기를 담았어요.
examples.en: This novel tells the stories of nameless common people.

examples.ko: 민초는 잡초처럼 밟혀도 다시 일어난다고 말해요.
examples.en: They say common people rise again like weeds even when trampled.
Politicians should know the hardships of ordinary people.
It is important to hear the voices of ordinary people.

examples.ko: 역사책에는 왕만 나오지만 민초가 나라를 지켰어요.
examples.en: History books mention only kings, but ordinary people protected the country.

explain: '백성'을 질기게 자라나는 풀에 빗댄 말로, 글이나 뉴스에서 평범한 서민을 따뜻하게 부를 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '서민', '평범한 사람들'이라고 말하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: Nameless common people protected the country.
phrases.nuance_ko: 역사 속의 평범한 사람들을 높이는 말로 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a common phrase that honors ordinary people in history.

phrases.en: When prices go up, ordinary people suffer the most.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '민초' 대신 더 많이 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is used much more than 민초 in everyday conversation.

phrases.example: 이 책에는 민초들의 삶이 생생하게 담겨 있어요.
phrases.en: This book vividly captures the lives of common people.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의'를 붙여 '삶', '이야기' 같은 말과 함께 글에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '의', it often pairs with words like 삶 (life) or 이야기 (story) in writing.

explain_en: It compares common people to resilient grass and is used in writing and news to refer warmly to ordinary folk. In daily conversation people more often say '서민' or '평범한 사람들'.

t90.ax: The lives of ordinary people have never been easy.

en: to be alienated; to be marginalized; to be excluded

examples.en: I'm upset because my friends leave only me out.
Please don't deliberately leave anyone out.

examples.ko: 그 팀장은 새 직원을 소외시킨 적이 없어요.
examples.en: That team leader has never shut out a new employee.

examples.ko: 약한 사람을 소외시키는 사회는 좋지 않아요.
examples.en: A society that pushes weak people aside is not a good one.
The kids played while shutting one friend out.
They will push out the people who object.

explain: '소외당하다'와 짝이에요. 끼워 주지 않는 쪽이 주어일 때 이 말을 쓰고, 당하는 쪽이 주어일 때는 '소외당하다'를 써요. '따돌리다'는 더 일상적이고 직접적인 말이에요.

phrases.en: His friends shut him out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 일상적이고 직접적인 말로, 무리에 끼워 주지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more everyday, direct word for refusing to include someone.

phrases.example: 신입 직원을 소외시키지 않으려고 먼저 말을 걸었어요.
phrases.en: I spoke first so as not to leave the new employee out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 써서 모두를 함께 챙긴다는 뜻을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form shows that everyone is being included.

phrases.en: I dislike an atmosphere that leaves someone out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 쓰면 무리의 분위기를 비판하는 말이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a noun, it criticizes the mood of a group.

explain_en: This is the partner of 소외당하다. Use it when the subject is the one leaving others out; use 소외당하다 when the subject is the one left out. 따돌리다 is more everyday and more direct.

t90.ax: They will push out the people who object.

examples.en: The party's young reformers demanded reform.
He is called one of the young scholars in academia.
The young lawmakers gathered and held a press conference.
At a company too, the opinions of the younger faction matter.
There is conflict between the young faction and the elders.
Young directors called the new guard are getting attention.

explain: 어떤 조직이나 분야에서 젊고 개혁적인 사람들을 가리켜요. 나이 많은 쪽은 '원로'나 '중진'이라고 해서 대비해서 자주 나와요. 주로 정치나 학계 뉴스에서 보는 말이에요.

phrases.en: The young reformist lawmakers submitted a new bill.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정치 뉴스에서 가장 자주 보이는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The pairing seen most often in political news.

phrases.en: The opinions of the young reformists and the elders were very different.
phrases.nuance_ko: 젊은 쪽과 나이 많은 쪽을 대비할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to contrast the young side with the senior side.

phrases.en: The young reformist group announced a reform plan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 개혁을 원하는 젊은 사람들의 모임을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A group of young people who want reform.

explain_en: It refers to the young, reform-minded people within an organization or field. It is often contrasted with the older side, called '원로' or '중진'. You mostly see it in political or academic news.

en: to harass; to annoy; to give trouble

examples.ko: 아이가 밥을 안 먹어서 부모를 애먹여요.
examples.en: The child won't eat, so he gives his parents a hard time.
The mischievous puppy gave us a hard time.
Please don't give our team leader too much trouble.

examples.ko: 고장 난 컴퓨터가 계속 저를 애먹여요.
examples.en: The broken computer keeps giving me trouble.
My younger sibling hid on purpose to give me a hard time.

examples.ko: 이 문제는 몇 년째 우리를 애먹이고 있어요.
examples.en: This problem has been troubling us for years.

explain: 내가 고생하는 건 '애먹다', 남이나 어떤 일이 나를 고생시키는 건 '애먹이다'예요. 사람뿐 아니라 고장 난 물건이나 어려운 문제도 주어가 될 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 컴퓨터가 계속 애를 먹여서 일을 못 했어요.
phrases.en: The computer kept giving me trouble, so I couldn't work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 띄어 써도 같은 뜻이고, 어려움을 주는 상대를 주어로 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning when spaced; the subject is whoever causes the difficulty.
phrases.en_equiv: to give someone a hard time

phrases.en: The son keeps worrying his parents.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주로 사람이 걱정과 근심을 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Mostly used when a person causes worry and anxiety.

phrases.en: Please stop giving me such a hard time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘들게 하지 말라고 부탁하거나 말릴 때 쓰는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A conjugated form used to ask someone to stop causing trouble.
phrases.en_equiv: don't give me a hard time

explain_en: '애먹다' is when you suffer yourself, while '애먹이다' is when someone or something causes you trouble. The subject can be a person, a broken object or a hard problem.
